sentences.text: Dr. Amit Bhatia, learned Govt. Advocate for the respon  ORDER 1.

By this petition preferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India the petitioner has prayed for the following reliefs :-
"(a) That Hon'ble High Court may kindly be pleased to allow the writ petition and issue a writ of mandamus directing the respondent No.2 to release the petitioner's vehicles (Buses) bearing registration No.MP09S-0834 and MP13K-2700 has been seized by the authority of respondent No.2 on 18.06.2005 and till date the same are lying idol in Police Station Hatpipaliya.
( b) Any other appropriate orders against respondents be issued in favour of the petitioner with cost of the petition."

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that on account of registration of a criminal case against the petitioner on 03.11.2010 under Section 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the IPC the vehicle of the petitioner was confiscated by the respondents.
Thereafter upon completion of the investigation charge-sheet was filed before the Court concerned where charges were framed on 21.12.2022.

However by order dated 30.12.2023 the Court concerned returned the final charge-sheet to the Economic Offence Wing, Indore for filing the same NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

It is further submitted that thereafter no charge-sheet has been filed before any Court of law as a result of which as of now there is no pending criminal case against the petitioner.

The petitioner had made an application before the criminal Court also for grant of custody of the vehicle to him but the said application has been rejected on the ground that there is no case pending.

3. From the documents which have been brought on record it is evident that investigation was initially conducted against the petitioner and charge-sheet was filed but the same was returned for being presented before the competent Court which has not been done as yet.
At best there is only an investigation pending as of now.
The vehicle of the petitioner was seized almost 15 years ago and must have already deteriorated considerably by now.
It would be wholly unjust to keep the same in custody any further particularly when the prosecution agency has itself not taken any interest in proceeding against the petitioner.

4. Consequently it is directed that the custody of the vehicle of the petitioner bearing registration No.MP-09-S-0834 and MP-13-K-2700 be handed over to the petitioner by the concerned Police Station within a period of 15 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
5.
With the aforesaid direction, petition stands disposed off.
